question: Which coal sample had the largest porosity increase after the oxidation treatment for coalbed methane, and what moisture and ash contents did it have?
rendered:

The change in porosity of samples LRC-XJ-A, LRC-XJ-B, and MRC-SX-A exceeded 15% (Table 3). The largest increase in porosity was 48.54% for sample HRC-SX-C, however it was not among the samples that exceeded 15%. The porosity of sample HRC-SX-C before the oxidation treatment was 3.09% (Table 2). 

[Alterations in Coal Permeability and Adsorption Capacity Post Oxidation Treatment: Insights into Enhancing Coalbed Methane Production, page 9]
Variations in Permeability/Wettability and Coal Properties The varying changes in k0 indicated that reservoir parameters had an essential impact on the oxidation treatment. The reduction in SSA after the oxidation treatment promoted more gas desorption at the same pressure, accelerating the CBM production. However, the decreasing CA was not conducive to water production from the reservoir, which is detrimental to the CBM production. Therefore, the relationship between the changes in k0/CA and the reservoir parameters was clarified. As the permeability and wettability changed due to organic matter corrosion, the relationship among Mad + Ad/molecular structure/porosity and the change in k0/CA was discussed in this study. Coal generally comprises organic matter, a small amount of minerals, and moisture, with the Ad reflecting the mineral content. Consequently, Mad + Ad is indicative of the nonorganic matter content of the coal. The change in k0/CA was positively correlated with Mad + Ad, with the change in k0/ CA mostly less than 100% when the Mad + Ad exceeded 20% (Figure 11a,b).
